description: MapSwipe is a mobile and web app in which volunteers swipe through satellite and street-level image tiles to say where features such as buildings, roads and waterways are, to compare images before and after an event, and to check the quality of existing mapping. Humanitarian organisations set up projects in an admin interface, back-end workers split them into groups of tiles, and results sync back and are published openly. Project types include find features, compare dates, validate footprints, check completeness, assess image, view streets and locate objects; results of find features projects are ready to use in the HOT Tasking Manager. When read, the data page reported 222 million swipes by 143,000 contributors and was updated on 27 September 2026. Coverage: projects worldwide. Access: free apps and a public data page with per-project files. Licence: Apache 2.0 for the app code; the data are open with credit to contributors. Caveats: results are crowd judgements on imagery and need aggregation. Simulation uses are finding where buildings exist to target mapping, damage screening after disasters and validating machine-learned footprints for exposure models. Related records: the HOT Tasking Manager, OpenStreetMap and the DLR World Settlement Footprint.
